newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng Bank sees 1997 Hong Kong GDP up 5.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank sees 1997 Hong Kong GDP up 5.4 pct.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank said on Thursday it forecast Hong Kong's gross domestic product would grow 5.4 percent in 1997 as a recovering world economy, a steady dollar and improving domestic demand underpinned an overall pick-up.
For 1996, the government has forecast 4.7 percent growth in GDP.
The bank said that with more economic growth, the inflation rate would rise moderately to 7.0 percent in the coming year, against this year's official forecast of 6.0 percent.
The unemployment rate is expected to fall to 2.5 percent, it said in a report.
The report also forecast that with a gradual recovery in the global economy, Hong Kong's total exports would grow at a rate of 9.7 percent in 1997, up from 5.4 percent in 1996.

But it said the long-term outlook for exports would be affected by changes in trade flows due to the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and the development of port facilites in southern China leading to a loss in the territory's re-export business.
Rallies in the property and stock markets are expected to have a small wealth effect, it said.
Private consumption expenditure is expected to increase by 4.8 percent, only moderately higher than the official estimate of 4.0 percent for 1996, the report said.
